### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/architecture.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_
- `content/docs/plugins/development.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface SeedReadinessHost))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 50 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **55** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f588614e6e62e64ce5664119b99876a673770259` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b8a968c232807c2900d7e736df2976a9286a90b3` — the merge of head `7350d54ff6c679df4ab95ee00a5da131eaba2349` into base `f588614e6e62e64ce5664119b99876a673770259`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b8a968c232807c2900d7e736df2976a9286a90b3 && git checkout b8a968c232807c2900d7e736df2976a9286a90b3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f588614e6e62e64ce5664119b99876a673770259 7350d54ff6c679df4ab95ee00a5da131eaba2349 && git checkout -B drift-repro f588614e6e62e64ce5664119b99876a673770259 && git merge --no-ff 7350d54ff6c679df4ab95ee00a5da131eaba2349

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f588614e6e62e64ce5664119b99876a673770259
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f588614e6e62e64ce5664119b99876a673770259` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review: PASS

Head: `7350d54ff6c679df4ab95ee00a5da131eaba2349` · reviewer review#2 (`session_016WV4cxDxAYxdtDhtR1kQQe`) · area A4 · Fixes #33233

Checked:
- `readSeedReadiness` reads the two records the kernel already keeps. `pending` keys on `inFlight > 0`, and `declareSeedSource` counts a source as in flight from the moment it is declared in `AppPlugin.start()` (`app-plugin.ts`, before the inline / deferred / suppressed branch). So a seed deferred to `kernel:bootstrapped` (demo staff, seed files) reads `pending`, not a false `settled`, in the gap before it starts. Suppression decrements `inFlight`, so multi-tenant and `skipSeedData` read `settled` as documented.
- `seedOutcomeIsClean` matches the IPC `ok` predicate in `composeSeedSettledMessage` (`rejected === 0 && droppedRefs === 0 && !emptyInstall`), so HTTP and IPC agree.
- `/ready`: the reading is on the host kernel (`this.defaultKernel`, #5155), it is taken per probe, both 200 branches get it, the status code is unchanged, and the 503 envelopes are untouched. With no tracker the body object is returned as given (no key), so non-seeding deployments see the old body. The route is ledgered `server-only` with no `responseSchema`.
- CLI: `noteBanner` records the snapshot the banner printed, and `settled` prints once only when that snapshot was in flight. A settle before the banner, `--json` (no banner thunk) and a second settle all print nothing. The print goes to stderr, and a throw is swallowed so it cannot cost the IPC send.
- Tests pin pending → settled on the same dispatcher (not cached), any-source-in-flight, failed (rejected / dropped ref / empty install) still 200, settled with no outcome, suppression, the degraded-secondary body and the 503. Ablations are recorded for both legs.
- `Clause-②: no` accepted: no export moves (`seed-readiness.ts` is not re-exported from the runtime root; `printSeedResultAfterBanner` lives in cli `utils/format.ts`, outside the `exports` map), and the only external change is an additive key on a server-only probe body with no declared schema. Runtime and cli patch is right.

Nits (optional, no card owed):
- N1: the clean-seed predicate now has a fourth spelling (the PR notes this). Exporting `seedOutcomeIsClean` and having `composeSeedSettledMessage` use it would take that down to one, in a later PR.
- N2: CI was still running at review time. Landing needs every check green on this head, as usual.
